info.title: dflockd HTTP API
info.summary: REST + SSE interface to dflockd's distributed lock, semaphore, and signal primitives.
info.description:
dflockd is a lightweight distributed lock server with FIFO ordering, automatic lease expiry, semaphores, and NATS-style pub/sub signals. This HTTP API is a translation layer over the native line-based TCP protocol: every HTTP session owns an in-process virtual connection that feeds the unchanged protocol handler, so FIFO ordering, lease handling, two-phase acquire, and configured disconnect cleanup are identical across transports.

## Session model

The native protocol ties lock ownership to a TCP connection. HTTP has no such connection, so the bridge introduces a **session** abstraction:

1. `POST /v1/sessions` mints a server-generated opaque ID and allocates a virtual connection server-side.
2. Every subsequent request carries `X-Dflockd-Session: <id>` so the bridge routes it to the correct virtual connection. Two-phase `enqueue`/`wait` flows therefore work the same way they do over TCP.
3. `DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}` closes the virtual connection synchronously, triggering the same cleanup path as a TCP disconnect. With default `--auto-release-on-disconnect`, this releases held locks and semaphore slots immediately; if that setting is disabled, held resources remain until explicit release or lease expiry.

## Keeping sessions alive

The virtual connection has a read timeout (server-configured via `--read-timeout`, default 23s). Any HTTP operation on a session resets that deadline, so an actively-used session stays alive. If a lock or semaphore session is otherwise idle, the client should call `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/ping` to keep the virtual connection from being torn down. SSE streams use a dedicated internal session with server-side protocol pings, so SSE clients do not ping sessions themselves.

## Lease renewal

Acquire returns a `token` and a `lease_ttl_s`. If the client doesn't `POST .../renew` before the TTL expires, the server reclaims the lock and transfers it to the next waiter. Typical clients renew at ~1/3 of the TTL.

## Crash safety

If an HTTP client dies without calling `DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}`, the bridge cleans up when the virtual connection read timeout fires or when the idle session sweeper closes the session after roughly 2× `--http-session-idle-timeout`; active in-flight commands are not swept. With auto-release on disconnect enabled, held locks and semaphore slots are released when the virtual connection closes. With auto-release disabled, rely on explicit release or lease expiry.

## Cross-transport interop

The HTTP bridge and the TCP protocol share a single `LockManager`, so an HTTP session and a TCP client contending on the same key are ordered together in the same FIFO queue.

See the [architecture docs](https://mtingers.github.io/dflockd/architecture/overview/) for the full model.

tags.name: sessions
tags.description: Create, ping, and close HTTP sessions. A session is the HTTP analogue of a persistent TCP connection.

tags.name: locks
tags.description: Exclusive lock primitives. Each key has at most one holder at a time. Acquires are FIFO-ordered across all transports.

tags.name: semaphores
tags.description: Counted semaphore primitives. Up to `limit` concurrent holders per key. The first acquirer sets the limit; subsequent calls must match.

tags.name: signals
tags.description: Publish/subscribe message delivery with NATS-style wildcards (`*`, `>`) and optional queue groups.

post.description:
Mints a server-generated opaque session ID and opens a virtual connection into the protocol handler. The returned `session_id` must be sent in the `X-Dflockd-Session` header on every subsequent request that touches lock or semaphore state.

The `idle_timeout_s` in the response is an advisory heartbeat target: otherwise idle lock and semaphore sessions should ping well before it elapses, for example halfway through the interval. The bridge will tolerate idle periods up to about 2× this before reaping the session, but the virtual connection's `--read-timeout` is still the protocol deadline.

delete.description:
Synchronously closes the virtual connection associated with this session. Signal subscriptions, pending waiters, and two-phase enqueue state are removed. With default `--auto-release-on-disconnect`, held locks and semaphore slots are released immediately and passed to the next FIFO waiter. If that setting is disabled, held resources remain until explicit release or lease expiry.

This is the explicit-cleanup path. If a client crashes without calling DELETE, cleanup happens later via virtual connection read timeout or the idle-session sweeper.

post.description:
No-op protocol command that resets the virtual connection's read deadline. Call periodically when the session is otherwise idle to prevent the server from reaping it.

Any other command on a session (acquire, renew, etc.) also serves as a heartbeat, so explicit pings are only needed when regular commands will not happen before the idle timeout. SSE streams use their own dedicated server-pinged session.

get.description:
Returns a snapshot of the server's active locks, semaphores, waiter queues, idle entries awaiting GC, signal subscriptions, and active protocol connections. Sessionless — does not require `X-Dflockd-Session`.

Note that gathering stats briefly locks every shard, so don't poll this endpoint faster than once per second in production.

post.description:
Single-phase exclusive lock acquire. The call blocks on the server side until the lock is free (FIFO) or `acquire_timeout_s` elapses.

On success, the response carries a `token` that must be presented on future `release` and `renew` calls. On timeout, the response is still HTTP 200 with `status: "timeout"` — it's a domain outcome, not a transport error.

The server's `--default-lease-ttl` is used if `lease_ttl_s` is omitted or zero.

Release a held lock. The token must match the current holder. On success, the lock passes to the next FIFO waiter (if any). On token mismatch (e.g. the lease expired and was reclaimed), returns 404 `not_held`.

404.description: Token doesn't match the current holder (may have expired and been reassigned)

post.description:
Extend the lease on a currently-held lock. The new expiry is `now + lease_ttl_s`, or `now + --default-lease-ttl` if `lease_ttl_s` is omitted or zero. If the token no longer matches the current holder, returns 404 `not_held`.

Clients should renew at ~1/3 of the lease TTL to survive network hiccups without dropping the lock.

404.description: Token mismatch or lease already expired

post.description:
First step of two-phase lock acquisition. Joins the FIFO queue and returns **immediately** (non-blocking).

If the lock was free, the response is `status: "acquired"` with a token — the lease is already running. If it was busy, `status: "queued"` and the caller must follow up with `POST .../wait` to block until granted.

Between `enqueue` and `wait`, the caller can run arbitrary application logic (notify external systems, check preconditions, etc.) without holding up other FIFO positions.

200.description: Either acquired on fast path, or queued

409.description: Session already has a pending enqueue for this key

post.summary: Wait for a queued lock (two-phase step 2)
post.description:
Second step of two-phase lock acquisition. Blocks on the same session that issued the `enqueue` until the lock is granted or `timeout_s` expires.

On success, the lease is reset to `now + lease_ttl_s` (the TTL from the original enqueue), so the caller gets the full TTL from the moment `wait` returns.

If the session has no outstanding enqueue for this key, returns 409 `not_enqueued`. If the lease expired before the waiter consumed the grant (e.g. network delay after the grant was sent), returns 409 `lease_expired`.

409.description: No pending enqueue, or lease already expired

post.description:
Single-phase semaphore acquire. Blocks until a slot is free or `acquire_timeout_s` elapses.

The first acquirer of a semaphore key sets the `limit`. Every subsequent request must pass the same limit or receive 409 `limit_mismatch`.

Semaphore keys are in a separate namespace from lock keys — using the same key string for a lock and a semaphore creates two independent resources.

409.description: Limit doesn't match the existing semaphore's limit

post.description: Release a held semaphore slot. Token must match one of the current holders. Frees the slot for the next FIFO waiter.
Extend the lease on a held semaphore slot. Same semantics as lock renew.
Two-phase semaphore enqueue. See `/v1/locks/{key}/enqueue` — semaphore semantics are identical except that up to `limit` concurrent slots are granted.

post.summary: Wait for a queued semaphore slot
post.description: Second step of two-phase semaphore acquisition. Same semantics as lock wait.

Publish a signal on a literal channel. The channel name **must not** contain the wildcard characters `*` or `>`. The payload is delivered to every matching listener (exact subscriptions, wildcard subscriptions, and queue groups) according to the same delivery rules as the TCP `signal` command.

This endpoint is **sessionless** — the bridge creates a transient internal session for the duration of the call. Use it from webhook handlers, cron jobs, or any context where you don't want to manage a session.

Returns the count of listeners the signal was delivered to.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: Literal channel name (dot-separated tokens). Must not contain `*` or `>`.

get.description:
Open a long-lived SSE stream of signals matching `pattern`. Patterns support NATS-style wildcards (`*` matches one token, `>` matches one or more trailing tokens).

The bridge opens a **dedicated session** for the lifetime of the stream, so the internal pinger (configured by `--http-sse-ping-interval`, default 15s) doesn't contend with any commands on the caller's other session. When the HTTP client disconnects (client-initiated close, network drop, or server shutdown), the bridge unregisters the listen subscription and tears down the session.

Each matched signal is sent as one SSE frame:

```
event: sig
data: {"channel": "...", "payload": "..."}
```

Client libraries should follow SSE reconnection semantics — the server sends no `id:` field, so reconnection restarts from "now".

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Subscription pattern. Exact channel (`events.user.login`) or wildcard (`events.*`, `events.>`).

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Queue group name. Within a group, each matching signal is delivered to exactly one member (round-robin).

get.description: Returns this document. Exempt from authentication so tools and clients can fetch the schema without credentials.

bearerAuth.description: Shared secret configured via `--auth-token` / `DFLOCKD_AUTH_TOKEN`. When set, every request (except `GET /v1/openapi.json`) must carry `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. When unset, authentication is disabled and the header is ignored.

SessionHeader.name: X-Dflockd-Session
SessionHeader.description: Opaque session ID returned by `POST /v1/sessions`. Ties the request to a specific virtual connection so two-phase flows and lock ownership work correctly.

KeyPath.name: key
KeyPath.description: Lock or semaphore key. Must be non-empty and contain no whitespace. URL-encode any special characters.

BadRequest.description: Malformed request (bad JSON, missing field, invalid parameter, etc.)

SessionGone.description: Session ID doesn't resolve — either never existed or was swept/closed

CapacityExceeded.description: Server resource limit hit (max_locks, max_waiters, max_sessions)

session_id.description: Opaque session identifier. Pass in `X-Dflockd-Session` on future requests.

idle_timeout_s.description: Advisory heartbeat target; otherwise idle lock and semaphore sessions should ping well before this many seconds elapse.

acquire_timeout_s.description: How long to wait for the lock in seconds. 0 = fail-fast.

lease_ttl_s.description: Lease duration. If omitted or 0, uses the server's `--default-lease-ttl`.

limit.description: Maximum concurrent holders for this semaphore key. Must match the limit set by the first acquirer.

lease_ttl_s.description: Lease duration. If omitted or 0, uses the server's `--default-lease-ttl`.

status.description: `ok` means acquired; `timeout` means the request window elapsed without acquisition.

token.description: Lock token. Only present when status=ok.

lease_ttl_s.description: Lease duration in seconds. Only present when status=ok.

token.description: Token returned by the acquire/wait/enqueue call.

lease_ttl_s.description: New lease duration. If omitted or 0, uses server default.
Lease duration for when the grant eventually lands. If omitted or 0, uses server default.
Lease duration for when the grant eventually lands. If omitted or 0, uses server default.

status.description: `acquired` = fast path, lease is running; `queued` = must call `/wait`.

timeout_s.description: Max seconds to wait for the grant.

payload.description: Any non-empty UTF-8 string (no newlines). Typically a JSON-encoded object.

delivered.description: Count of listeners that received the signal (exact + wildcard + group deliveries).

connections.description: Active protocol connections visible to the HTTP API: TCP connections plus active HTTP sessions.
